import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    types = list(feats.types)
    x = feats.x
    y = feats.y
    
    # Build correlation matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(x.T)
    
    # Identify near-duplicates (|r| >= 0.6)
    to_remove = set()
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                to_remove.add(ids[j])
    
    # Filter out near-duplicates
    filtered_ids = [id for id in ids if id not in to_remove]
    filtered_indices = [i for i, id in enumerate(ids) if id not in to_remove]
    if len(filtered_indices) == 0:
        return Design(
            drivers=(),
            columns=(),
            products=(),
            loadings={}
        )
    filtered_x = x[:, filtered_indices]
    
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(filtered_ids):
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        group0 = x[y==0, idx]
        group1 = x[y==1, idx]
        effect = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
        effect_sizes.append(abs(effect))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    sorted_idx = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    top_ids = [filtered_ids[i] for i in sorted_idx[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # Select top features for regression
    columns = tuple(top_ids)
    
    # Check for interactions among top features
    products = []
    if len(columns) >= 2:
        # Simple approach: look for strong correlations among top features
        top_indices = [feats.column(fid) for fid in columns]
        if len(top_indices) >= 2:
            top_corr = np.corrcoef(x[:, top_indices].T)
            
            # Add interaction terms between highly correlated top features
            for i in range(len(columns)):
                for j in range(i+1, len(columns)):
                    if abs(top_corr[i,j]) > 0.5:  # moderate correlation
                        products.append((columns[i], columns[j]))
    
    # Create loadings dictionary for weighted score
    loadings = {}
    for fid in columns:
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        # Use standardized coefficients from univariate associations
        group0 = x[y==0, idx]
        group1 = x[y==1, idx]
        effect = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
        loadings[fid] = effect
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(top_ids),
        columns=columns,
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
